RSV admissions rose to 1.66 per 100,000 and positivity to 5.2%, while COVID-19 was broadly stable at 2.22. Flu is above baseline and rising but not at high levels nationally, and no widespread NHS critical incidents were found as of 22 Nov, so Watch is kept.
nhs-pressure.for_you: Flu is rising earlier than usual. The NHS advises eligible people, including over-65s, pregnant women and those with long-term conditions, to get their flu and RSV vaccines.

private-credit.value: Nontraded BDC exit requests above 5% cap
private-credit.summary: Redemption requests at most nontraded BDCs stay above their 5% quarterly cap; no wave of gates or forced sales
private-credit.state: Fitch found that 13 of 15 perpetual nontraded BDCs received third-quarter redemption requests averaging 9.8% of shares, down from 10.3% in the second quarter but well above their 5% quarterly caps; Blue Owl Technology Income Corp faced requests for 39% (InvestmentNews, 13 Oct). Fitch warned in March that more semi-liquid funds may hold redemptions to their caps if the exit rush continues (Creditflux). Searches on 22 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, no forced asset sales and no losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
private-credit.for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may find withdrawals limited to a share of the fund each quarter. Wider stress would tend to show first in tighter lending to mid-sized companies.

em-stress.summary: Rupiah steady near record lows around 18,260/$ after Bank Indonesia's 18 Nov rate rise; no EM default or IMF rescue
em-stress.state: The rupiah closed at 18,255 per dollar on 19 Nov (Bisnis Indonesia), with a reference rate of 18,275 that day (Databoks), close to the record low near 18,290 set before Bank Indonesia raised its rate to 6% on 18 Nov. The currency has held roughly steady since the rise and is about 9% weaker this year, short of a 10% fall in a month. No major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 22 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
em-stress.for_you: A strong dollar and higher US rates keep pressure on emerging-market currencies, raising import costs and dollar-debt burdens there. Travellers to Indonesia get more rupiah per pound.

fertiliser.summary: Egyptian urea rose to $535 a tonne after gas cuts to plants; Hormuz flows near pre-war levels but tanker attacks go on
fertiliser.state: Egyptian granular urea rose to $535 a tonne FOB in November, about 17% above September's $457, after gas deliveries to nitrogen plants were cut by up to 20% from 1 Nov (UkrAgroConsult, 10 Nov). Shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels, though attacks on tankers continued at about one a day in November (The Edge Malaysia, 20 Nov). That is short of a 60% three-month rise, several exporters restricting at once or a closed route, so Watch holds.
fertiliser.for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring face higher prices from some suppliers, which can feed into crop costs and food prices later in 2027.

nuclear-plants.state: Zaporizhzhia lost off-site power for over 12 hours on 8 Nov and ran on emergency diesel generators (Ukrainska Pravda); it now relies on a single 330kV line (ANS, 19 Nov). IAEA Director General Grossi told the IAEA Board on 18 Nov that it would be difficult to overstate his concern about Ukraine's grid as winter sets in (ANS). Safety systems at other Ukrainian plants stayed operational, and no damage to safety-critical systems, INES level 2 event or radiological release was found as of 22 Nov.
nuclear-plants.for_you: There is no radiological risk to the UK. The IAEA's updates are the authoritative source on plant safety in Ukraine.

gulf-iran.summary: Qatari mediators met Iranian officials on 20–21 Nov; Iran calls the US blockade an act of war; no ceasefire or deal
gulf-iran.state: A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on 20 Nov, and Deputy Foreign Minister Gharibabadi said on 21 Nov the contacts are not yet formal negotiations and called the US blockade of Iranian ports an act of war (Al Jazeera). US envoys Witkoff and Kushner met Qatari mediators on 20 Nov (Axios). Lloyd's List Intelligence counted 550 non-Iranian Hormuz transits in October, the most since the war began, but seven attacks on ships on 5–11 Nov. Attacks on shipping and no ceasefire keep the Alert.
gulf-iran.for_you: Shipping, fuel and freight costs remain exposed to attacks around Hormuz. Travellers to the Gulf should follow FCDO travel advice, which can change at short notice.

medicine-shortages.summary: UK pharmacists say shortages hit up to 6.4m items a month; a flood-hit plant may prolong US chemo shortages to 2028
medicine-shortages.state: On 17 Nov the National Pharmacy Association estimated shortages could affect up to 6.4 million prescription items a month in 2026 (Pharmaceutical Journal). In the US, ASHP counted 225 active shortages in the third quarter, with cancer drug shortages worsening (Becker's Hospital Review), and a flood-damaged plant may prolong chemotherapy shortages to 2028 (CancerNetwork, 2 Nov). Shortages span several countries but no widespread rationing across major health systems was found on 22 Nov, so Watch holds.
medicine-shortages.for_you: If a pharmacy cannot supply a medicine, speak to the pharmacist or GP about alternatives; do not stop treatment without advice. NHS guidance covers Serious Shortage Protocols that let pharmacists substitute.
